source_references.citation: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012), Time Series Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 104(2)
source_references.supports: Own past futures excess-return sign predicts subsequent return in the studied sample; the source strategy is not this ETF adaptation.

source_references.citation: Huang, Li, Wang and Zhou (2020), Time Series Momentum: Is It There?, Journal of Financial Economics 135
source_references.supports: Counterevidence on asset-level, pooled, and out-of-sample predictability.

source_references.citation: Huang and Huang (2020), Testing Moving Average Trading Strategies on ETFs, Journal of Empirical Finance 57
source_references.supports: Caution that tradable ETF implementations can differ materially from index evidence.

research.evidence_summary: The source evidence is for diversified futures/forwards strategies. This fixed seven-ETF long/cash rule removes the short leg and volatility scaling and is a proposed retail adaptation with meaningful published counterevidence.

feasibility.rationale: Operationally simple in a portfolio system, but V2 lacks the required adjusted ETF data, cash series, target weights, next-open portfolio rebalance, and stopless return accounting.

market.session: Each ETF's official US regular trading session, including official early closes

data.frequency: Daily observations plus official month-end markers
data.minimum_history: All seven ETFs with twelve complete prior month-ends; common tradable start no earlier than DBC availability
preprocessing: Build point-in-time split/dividend-consistent total-return levels without future corporate-action leakage
Retain raw executable next-session opens separately
Apply each instrument's exchange calendar and mark stale/missing data
dependencies: Three-month Treasury-bill or predeclared cash total-return series
limitations: Fixed surviving ETFs introduce selection risk
DBC embeds futures roll and product effects
Current V2 cache does not establish these ETF/corporate-action/cash inputs

hypothesis.behavior: An ETF with a positive total return over the preceding twelve complete month-end intervals has a higher next-month return or provides a useful exposure filter relative to holding it continuously.
hypothesis.mechanism: Medium-horizon persistence could reflect gradual information diffusion or slow-moving capital, but the mechanism is not causally established; long/cash may work mainly by reducing left-tail exposure.
works_when: Cross-asset trends persist longer than one rebalance interval
Turnover and open slippage are small relative to the conditional-return difference
fails_when: Total-return signals or next-open execution data are biased
Cash and trading costs erase any exposure-filter benefit
falsifiable_predictions: Out-of-sample next-month returns after positive signals exceed returns after nonpositive signals
Net risk-adjusted performance exceeds the frozen equal-weight benchmark
Maximum drawdown is at least 20 percent lower than the frozen equal-weight benchmark

definitions.name: R12_i_m
definitions.formula: TRI[i,m] / TRI[i,m-12] - 1, using official month-end total-return levels
definitions.timing: Computed only after the final official regular-session close of month m

definitions.name: target_weight_i_m
definitions.timing: Target for the first regular-session open of month m+1

definitions.name: cash_weight_m
definitions.timing: Accrues the predeclared cash total-return series until the next rebalance

entries.long_condition: At month-end m, valid_data_i AND R12_i_m > 0 AND current_weight_i < 1/7
entries.signal_time: After the final official regular-session close of month m and after corporate-action-consistent data for that close are available
entries.execution_details: First executable regular-session open of month m+1; never the signal close
entries.order_type: Market-on-open proxy using raw executable open with declared spread/slippage
restrictions: No entry with missing/stale signal or executable price
Fractional shares required; otherwise predeclare deterministic floor rounding and retain residual cash

exits.time_exit: At the next monthly first-session open when target weight becomes zero or decreases
exits.signal_exit: R12_i_m <= 0 or invalid required data at a rebalance
exits.maximum_holding: Until the next monthly rebalance decision
priority: Invalid/delisted instrument liquidation under a separately reviewed data rule

risk.position_sizing: Fixed 1/7 portfolio sleeve per ETF when active; inactive sleeves accrue cash return
risk.concurrent_positions: At most seven long ETF positions; weights sum to no more than one

experiment.baseline: One frozen seven-ETF universe, 12-month signal, next-open monthly rebalance, 10 bps one-way changed-notional cost, cash return included
robustness_tests: Report each sleeve and long/cash exposure separately
Exclude the largest one percent of monthly portfolio returns
Compare point-in-time total-return and price-only diagnostic signals
Block-bootstrap paired performance differences by month
costs: Charge spread, slippage, commission and fees on both purchases and sales
Baseline 10 bps per one-way changed notional with 5 and 25 bps stresses
ETF expense and roll drag remain embedded in total returns
benchmarks: Monthly rebalanced 1/7 equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same seven ETFs using identical execution and costs
experiment.multiple_testing: Log all three lookbacks, cost stresses, delay, cash, and leave-one-out variants; do not promote the best diagnostic; adjust inferential families or use a synchronized block max-statistic.
rejection_criteria: Any unresolved corporate-action, stale-price, or executable-open audit failure
Untouched test has nonpositive net delta Sharpe and no drawdown improvement versus equal-weight
Benefit fails at 25 bps one-way costs or one-session delay
Benefit vanishes in leave-one-out tests or is dominated by one ETF or episode
Insufficient common history for a defensible test

pseudocode: After each official month-end close, compute each valid ETF's R12 from point-in-time total-return levels
Set each next-month target to 1/7 if R12 is positive, else zero
At the next regular-session open, trade changed notional to each target and charge two-sided realized costs
Accrue inactive and residual weight on the declared cash series
Mark all holdings and cash daily; record every diagnostic variant without selection
implementation.computational_requirements: Low compute; correctness of point-in-time data and portfolio accounting dominates runtime.
known_backtester_gaps: Order requires stop_loss and R-based accounting
No faithful stopless daily mark-to-market portfolio path
